title: Claude Code plugin manifest
description: Contract for src/claude/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, the framework's identity as the harness reads it. Source, retrieved 2026-07-31 and cited in full in the decision to distribute as a Claude Code plugin: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins — the manifest lives at .claude-plugin/plugin.json, its `name` is the namespace every plugin skill is invoked under, and a plugin without `version` falls back to its commit SHA. What this record owns is fixed here: identity, description, version, and nothing the distribution already carries. additionalProperties is false because this is a file Siegard authors rather than one it reads — a typo here would ship a plugin the harness names differently, and nothing here relies on behaviour absent from the documentation on the date above.

name.description: The plugin identity, and the namespace the harness prepends to every skill it ships: a skill named `ingest-domain` is invoked as `/<name>:ingest-domain`. Kebab-case because it appears verbatim in that invocation. A skill therefore never carries the namespace in its own name: it is applied here, once, and a skill that repeated it would be invoked under it twice.

description.description: What the plugin is, for a consumer deciding whether to enable it. Not a changelog and not a capability list: what the install holds is read from the distribution itself, and a field restated in two records is a field that can disagree with itself.

version.description: The framework version, set explicitly. A plugin without one falls back to its commit SHA, which makes every commit a release and takes the framework's version out of the framework's hands. Semantic versioning: a consumer reads the major to mean that a contract it depends on changed shape, which is what the contract_version constants in schemas/ record per artifact. It moves whenever what ships moves, and that is the whole of the rule: this value is the only name a consumer's installed copy has, so two different trees of src/claude/ carrying one version make every report sent back — every measurement, every defect, every cost — name a framework nobody can resolve to what actually ran. It has happened: three distinct shipped trees went out under one version, and the telemetry that came back from the third could not say it was the third. Nothing validates this; the value is set by whoever ships, and setting it is part of shipping rather than a step after it.
